the generation of a new type of soft‐tissue flap for the reconstruction of complex composite defects.
the development of an alternative to conventional microsurgical tissue transfer.
the development of a new, innovative, and promising technique to treat complex bone‐exposing soft‐tissue defects in the future.

the use of the AV loop‐based flap for reconstruction of composite defects is promising and that the model described here can be used as an alternative to conventional flaps.
the AV loop flap model is suitable for closure of complex composite defects in a standardized rat model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AV loop‐generated tissue represents an innovative and promising alternative to conventional free tissue flaps.
AV loops can be used to generate axially vascularized tissues that are capable of covering complex composite defects and can be transferred as free flaps.
the arteriovenous loop‐based flap model is a promising alternative to the conventional free flap model for reconstruction of critical defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AV loop model is a suitable tool for the creation and transfer of axially vascular soft‐tissue flaps.
AV loops can be used to create large volumes of vascularized tissue that can be transferred as free flaps to cover critical bone‐exposed defects in standardized animal models.
AV loop‐generated tissue is an attractive alternative for the treatment of critical defects.
